bayts.text: They said to me: "Lean on the doors of the sultans, you will obtain gifts that will make you rich for all time".
Then I said: "My Lord suffices me, and with Him I have been content, and I am not pleased (with anything) but the best of knowledge and religion".
And I neither hope in nor fear any but my King, for He — exalted be He — enriches me and saves me.
How should I entrust my states to those who are powerless over the state of their own souls, with the powerlessness of the destitute?
Or how could love of fleeting goods drive me to the neighbourhood of those whose dwellings are the garden of the devils?
If I am stricken with sorrow, or if I have a need, I call upon the Lord of the ʿAyn before the Rā and the Shīn (al-ʿArsh, the Throne).
And He is the Helper Whom nothing can render powerless, and He is the One Who brings into being what He wills, in whatever manner of bringing into being.
If He wills to hasten an affair, it is swift; or if He wills to defer it, it is delayed until (its) time.
O you who blame, do not overdo it, and leave your reproach, for I am not saddened by the loss of the world.
If my fault is detachment from their fleeting goods, that is a precious fault that does not disgrace me.
